hops.evidence: Water vapour cools and condenses into droplets that form clouds.
Droplets in clouds coalesce until gravity pulls them out as rain.
Solar heating evaporates surface water into water vapour.
Condensed water vapour returns to the surface as precipitation.
Iron reacts with oxygen in an oxidation reaction.
Oxidation of iron produces iron oxides known as rust.
Water accelerates the electrochemical oxidation of iron.
The oxidation reaction corrodes the metal.
The Moon exerts gravitational pull on Earth's oceans.
Differential lunar gravity raises ocean bulges that produce tides.
A battery's chemical reaction separates charge and drives electrons through a circuit.
The movement of electrons is an electric current.
A battery converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy.
Delivered electrical energy provides power to a device.
The Moon's mass produces gravitational attraction.
The Moon's gravity is the main driver of Earth's tides.
Chlorophyll absorbs energy from sunlight.
That captured energy drives the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
Photosynthesis supplies plants with the sugars they use for growth.
Plants release oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis.
Rain that does not soak into the ground becomes surface runoff.
Runoff collects in channels that form rivers.
Cooling air reduces its capacity to hold water vapour, causing condensation.
Condensed droplets suspended in air form clouds.
Uneven solar heating creates differences in air pressure.
Air moves from high to low pressure, which is wind.
Rising magma accumulates gas and pressure beneath the surface.
When pressure exceeds the strength of overlying rock, a volcanic eruption occurs.
Moving tectonic plates build elastic stress along faults.
Sudden fault slip releases the accumulated stress as an earthquake.
Hydrogen fusion in the Sun's core releases energy that emerges as sunlight.
Sunlight drives photosynthesis in plants.
Gravity provides the centripetal force that keeps planets in orbit.
Orbital geometry together with axial tilt gives rise to seasons.
Lowering water temperature below its freezing point causes freezing.
Frozen water forms ice.
Heat gives water molecules enough energy to escape the liquid surface.
Evaporation removes the most energetic molecules and cools the remaining liquid.
Digestive enzymes break food molecules into smaller units.
The resulting small molecules can be absorbed through the intestinal wall.
Sleep supports the consolidation of newly learned memories.
Consolidated memories are more readily recalled.
Muscular work raises the demand for oxygen and increases heart rate.
A faster heartbeat increases blood circulation.
Sufficient heat brings fuel to its ignition temperature.
Ignition starts the self-sustaining combustion we call fire.
A vibrating object creates alternating pressure waves in the air.
These waves move the eardrum and are interpreted as sound.
Charge separation inside clouds creates a strong electric field.
When the field exceeds air's breakdown strength, a lightning discharge occurs.
Light entering water droplets is refracted and split into component wavelengths.
Dispersed light reflected from droplets appears as a rainbow.
Rain produces moving surface water.
Moving water detaches and transports soil, causing erosion.
Sunlight powers the photosynthetic production of sugars.
Sugars provide the carbon skeletons and energy for growth.
Pathogens trigger an immune response.
Immune signalling raises the body's temperature set point, producing fever.
The Sun also exerts gravitational attraction on Earth's oceans.
Solar and lunar gravity align at new and full moon to produce spring tides.
Aligned electron spins produce a net magnetic field.
The field exerts force on ferromagnetic materials, causing attraction.
